st: Put the bones in a pot, cover with water and boil 10 minutes. Drain, rinse the bones and scrub the pot.
Char the onion and ginger directly over a flame or under the broiler until blackened in spots, about 5 minutes.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon and cloves in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return the bones to the pot with [[5 l]] water, brisket, onion, ginger and spices. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for [[3 hours]], skimming the foam. Remove the brisket after 1 hour and slice it.
Strain the broth. Season with [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] salt.
Soak the noodles in hot water for 20 minutes, then boil 1 to 2 minutes until tender. Drain.
Divide noodles between bowls and top with brisket and the raw sliced steak.
Pour boiling broth over the beef to cook it. Add cilantro, scallions, bean sprouts and lime.

ing: pork shoulder or tenderloin, sliced thin
st: Stir [[0.5 cup]] vinegar, [[0.5 cup]] warm water, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt until dissolved. Add the carrot and daikon.
Let the vegetables pickle for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the pork with [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and the garlic.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over high heat and cook the pork for 6 minutes until browned and cooked through to 145°F (63°C).
Warm the baguettes in a hot oven until crisp, then split them lengthwise.
Spread [[4 tbsp]] mayonnaise on one side and the pate on the other.
Fill with pork, drained pickles, cucumber, cilantro and chili.
Serve the sandwiches right away while the bread is crisp.
Mix the pork with [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, half the garlic, the shallot and [[1 tsp]] pepper. Marinate for [[30 minutes]].
Make the dipping broth: stir [[4 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[3 tbsp]] sugar, juice of 2 limes and [[1 cup]] warm water until dissolved.
Add the remaining garlic and chili to the broth.
Shape the pork into small patties, or thread slices on skewers.
Grill or pan-sear for 4 minutes per side until browned and cooked to 160°F (71°C).
Boil the vermicelli for 4 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain.
Place grilled pork in the dipping broth.
Serve noodles, lettuce and herbs on the side for dipping and eating together.
Boil the vermicelli for 4 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain well.
Set out all the fillings in bowls and a wide plate of warm water.
Dip a rice paper in warm water for 5 seconds until just soft, and lay on a damp board.
Line up 3 shrimp halves near the edge, then top with pork slices.
Add lettuce, noodles, mint and a chive on top.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly like a burrito.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] hoisin, [[1 tbsp]] peanut butter and [[2 tbsp]] warm water, then top with [[0.25 cup]] peanuts.
Serve with the dipping sauce.
Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes, drain and cut into short pieces.
Mix the pork, shrimp, carrot, noodles, onion, garlic, egg, [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Soften a rice paper in warm water for 5 seconds and place on a board.
Place about 2 tablespoons of filling near one corner.
Fold over the filling, tuck in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Repeat with the rest, keeping them from touching.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 340°F (170°C) in a deep pan.
Fry in batches for 8 minutes until golden and crisp and the pork reaches 160°F (71°C).
Drain on a rack and serve with lettuce, herbs and dipping sauce.

ing: pork hock or pork neck bones
st: Boil the beef and pork bones in water for 10 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Return to a pot with [[4 l]] water, onion and 3 stalks bruised lemongrass. Simmer [[2 hours]], skimming.
Mince the remaining 2 lemongrass stalks.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil, fry the minced lemongrass and [[2 tbsp]] chili flakes for 2 minutes.
Mix [[1 tbsp]] shrimp paste with a ladle of water and add it to the pot, with the chili oil.
Add [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer 20 minutes.
Remove the beef when tender, cool and slice thin.
Boil the noodles until soft, then drain.
Assemble noodles, beef and pork in bowls, ladle hot broth over, then top with herbs and lime.
Marinate the chops in [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, the lemongrass and half the garlic for [[30 minutes]].
Rinse [[2 cups]] rice, add [[3 cups]] water and cook in a covered pot on low for [[15 minutes]] until tender.
Heat the grill or pan with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Cook the chops 5 to 6 minutes per side until deep brown and 145°F (63°C) inside.
Fry the eggs in [[1 tbsp]] oil until the whites are set.
Warm the scallions in [[1 tbsp]] hot oil for 20 seconds to make scallion oil.
For the sauce, stir [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, remaining garlic and [[0.5 cup]] warm water.
Plate rice with a chop, an egg, cucumber and tomato. Drizzle with scallion oil and sauce.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] rice flour, [[1 cup]] coconut milk, [[1 cup]] water, [[1 tsp]] turmeric and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Stir in the scallions and rest the batter [[20 minutes]].
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook some pork slices and shrimp for 3 minutes until the pork is cooked.
Pour about [[0.75 cup]] batter into the pan and swirl it thin to coat.
Scatter bean sprouts over one half, cover and cook 3 minutes.
Uncover and cook another 3 minutes until the edges are crisp and golden.
Fold in half and slide to a plate. Repeat with the rest.
Wrap pieces in lettuce with herbs and dip in the sauce.
Marinate the fish in [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce, the garlic and [[1 tsp]] pepper for [[20 minutes]].
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a clay pot or heavy pan and cook the shallots 3 minutes.
Add [[0.25 cup]] sugar and cook until dark amber, about 5 minutes, without stirring.
Carefully add [[0.5 cup]] water, stir and bring to a boil.
Add the fish and [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce, plus the chili. Add [[0.5 cup]] more water.
Simmer gently, turning the fish once, for [[30 minutes]] until the sauce is thick and syrupy and the fish is cooked.
Sprinkle the sliced scallions over the top.
Serve the fish and sauce with [[4 cups]] hot cooked rice.
Marinate the beef with the lemongrass, garlic, [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[1 tbsp]] sugar for [[15 minutes]].
Boil the vermicelli for 4 minutes, rinse cold and drain.
Make the dressing: stir [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, juice of 2 limes and [[0.25 cup]] warm water.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wok over very high heat.
Stir-fry the beef for 3 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Divide lettuce, bean sprouts and herbs among bowls and top with noodles.
Top with the hot beef and drizzle with dressing.
Finish with [[0.25 cup]] peanuts.
Pour [[0.5 cup]] warm water into a bowl.
Add [[3 tbsp]] sugar and stir until it fully dissolves.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] lime juice.
Add the garlic and chili.
Taste and adjust: more sugar for sweeter, more lime for tangier.
Let it rest for [[5 minutes]] before serving with rolls, noodles or grilled meat.
Pour [[2 tbsp]] condensed milk into a heatproof glass.
Set a drip filter (phin) or small cone filter on top of the glass.
Add [[2 tbsp]] ground coffee and gently level it.
Pour in a little hot water to wet the grounds and wait 30 seconds.
Slowly add the remaining water from [[0.75 cup]] total, covering the filter.
Let it drip for about 5 minutes.
Stir the coffee and condensed milk together well.
Pour over [[1 cup]] ice in another glass and serve.
Mix flour, sugar, yeast and baking powder, add the warm water and knead 8 minutes into a smooth dough. Cover and rise 60 minutes.
Mix the pork, mushrooms, scallions and fish sauce. Cook in a skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes until no pink remains, then cool.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a 4 inch round, thinner at the edges.
Place a spoonful of filling and a piece of egg in the center of each round, then pleat the edges up and pinch closed at the top.
Set each bun on a square of parchment in a steamer, 2 inches apart, and rest 15 minutes.
Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes until puffed and white. Do not open the lid in the first 10 minutes.
nt: Steamed over boiling water
Best swap: replace the pork with crumbled firm tofu or extra mushrooms, same amount, to make it vegetarian.

st: Rinse [[0.33 cup]] tapioca pearls in a strainer under cold water. Bring [[3 cups]] water (and the pandan leaf if using) to a boil.
Add the tapioca and stir. Simmer on low for 12 minutes, stirring often so the pearls do not stick, until almost fully clear with a tiny white dot.
Stir in [[0.33 cup]] sugar and [[0.25 tsp]] salt until dissolved. Add the banana pieces and simmer gently 5 minutes until just tender but not mushy.
Pour in the coconut milk, reserving 4 tablespoons for topping. Heat 3 minutes without a hard boil, which could split the milk.
Remove the pandan leaf. Taste and add a little more sugar if needed.
Ladle into bowls and drizzle with the reserved coconut milk.
Top with [[2 tbsp]] crushed peanuts and [[1 tbsp]] toasted sesame. Serve warm or chilled.
nt: Simmered on the stovetop
Best swap: sago pearls for the tapioca pearls 1:1, and use plantains if you cannot find sweet firm bananas.

st: Drain the soaked mung beans and steam them in a heatproof dish over simmering water for 20 minutes until soft.
Mash the steamed mung beans with [[1 cup]] water and [[0.25 cup]] sugar in a small pot. Cook 5 minutes over low heat until thick like a paste.
Simmer the kidney beans with [[0.25 cup]] sugar and enough water to cover for 10 minutes. Drain and cool.
Warm the coconut milk with a pinch of salt for 3 minutes and cool.
In four tall glasses, layer the mung paste, then the kidney beans, then the jelly strips.
Fill each glass with crushed ice, pour coconut milk over, and serve right away with a long spoon.
nt: Steamed and simmered, served cold
Best swap: canned sweetened red beans or even sweet corn in place of kidney beans, any layer you prefer, and agar jelly for pandan jelly.

st: Cook the pork and shallots in a dry pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until the fat renders and the pork reaches 160°F. Add the shrimp and [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce and cook 3 minutes until pink. Cool.
Put the tapioca starch in a bowl. Pour in the boiling water gradually, stirring, until a soft dough forms. Knead 3 minutes while warm until smooth.
Roll the dough into 20 balls. Flatten each into a 3 inch round, thin at the edges.
Put a teaspoon of filling in each round. Fold into a half moon and press the edges to seal.
Steam on parchment or banana leaf over boiling water for 10 minutes, until the dumplings turn clear and chewy.
Mix [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce, the sugar, lime juice, garlic, chili and [[3 tbsp]] water for the dipping sauce.
Serve warm with the dipping sauce and fried shallots if you like.
nt: Steamed over boiling water
Best swap: use rehydrated minced shiitake and soy sauce in place of the shrimp, pork and fish sauce for a vegan version.

st: Wash the dragon fruit, mango, pineapple and watermelon under cold water, then dry the rinds so the cutting board stays clean and does not slip.
Cut the dragon fruit in half lengthwise and scoop out the whole flesh with a spoon. Slice into 1 cm half-moons. Keep one empty skin shell if you want a bowl.
Peel the pineapple, trim out the eyes in diagonal strips, then slice the pineapple into rings and cut each ring into 6 pieces.
Slice the mango cheeks away from the stone, peel, and cut into fat wedges. Cut the watermelon into neat triangles.
For the dip, grind [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] dried chili flakes with a mortar or fork until the mix is sandy and evenly red.
Peel the rambutan or lychee by pinching the skin and squeezing out the fruit. Chill all fruit for 15 minutes.
Arrange the fruit on a platter in rows of color, with the dip in a small saucer. Serve cold with picks.
nt: No cook: cut and arrange
Best swap: kiwi or honeydew for dragon fruit and canned lychee for fresh, drained and patted dry.

st: Halve 2 ripe avocados, remove the pits, and scoop the soft flesh into a blender.
Add [[4 tbsp]] sweetened condensed milk and [[0.5 cup]] cold milk if you want it looser.
Add [[1.5 cup]] ice cubes. Blend on high for 60 seconds until thick, creamy and pale green with no ice chunks.
Taste and blend in [[1 tbsp]] sugar if you want it sweeter.
Pour into tall glasses and serve at once with a spoon and a wide straw. It darkens and thickens if it waits.
nt: No cook: just blend
Best swap: use coconut condensed milk or 3 tbsp maple syrup with extra coconut milk for dairy-free.

st: Mix the pork, shrimp, egg, half the shallots, [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce and a pinch of pepper to a sticky paste. Chill for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Fry the remaining shallots for 1 minute, add the tomatoes, and cook 8 minutes until they break down.
Add the water, shrimp paste and the rest of the fish sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer, not a hard boil.
Drop spoonfuls of the pork and shrimp mixture into the broth. Simmer 10 minutes until they float and the pork is cooked through to 160°F.
Add the fried tofu and simmer 5 more minutes.
Cook the vermicelli in boiling water per the package, about 5 minutes, then drain and rinse. Divide into bowls, ladle the soup over, and top with sprouts and herbs.
nt: Simmered broth with poached meatballs
Best swap: crab paste or minced crab meat can replace the shrimp; use mushrooms and extra tofu for a vegetarian bowl with soy sauce.

st: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes to fully set, then cool in ice water and peel. Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes and rinse.
In a heavy pot, melt [[3 tbsp]] sugar over medium-low heat, without stirring, until amber, about 5 minutes. Watch it closely.
Add the shallots and garlic, then the pork. Stir for 5 minutes so the pork turns a deep golden brown.
Add [[3 cups]] coconut water, [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[1 tsp]] pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Cover with the lid ajar and simmer 40 minutes until the pork is tender and a fork slides in.
Add the peeled eggs and simmer uncovered 20 minutes, turning, until they are brown and the sauce is glossy.
Sprinkle with scallions and serve with rice and pickled mustard greens.
nt: Caramelized then slow braised
Best swap: soy sauce 2 tbsp plus 1 tbsp salt for fish sauce; use pork shoulder for belly.

st: Warm the baguettes in a 350°F oven for 4 minutes until the crust is crackly. Split each lengthwise, keeping one side attached.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and fry for about 3 minutes until the whites are set and the edges lacy and brown. Cook through, with no runny whites.
Stir the soy sauce and Maggi together in a small bowl. Spread the mayonnaise and pate on the cut sides of each loaf.
Lay the cucumber and cilantro in the bread, then add the pickled carrot and daikon, well drained.
Slide 2 fried eggs into each baguette and drizzle with the soy mixture. Add the chili slices.
Press the baguettes lightly to hold the filling and eat immediately while the bread is warm and the yolks are soft.
nt: Eggs pan-fried, bread oven-warmed
Best swap: use mushroom or vegetarian pate, or skip it and add sliced Vietnamese ham or grilled pork instead.

st: Toss the pork with [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, half the garlic, half the shallots and [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce. Marinate 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Fry the remaining shallots and garlic with the remaining turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the pork and sear 4 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes until pink. Remove the shrimp and set aside.
Pour in the stock and the remaining fish sauce. Simmer 15 minutes. You want just enough broth to coat the noodles, not a soup.
Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the package, usually 3 minutes for fresh. Drain.
Place a handful of lettuce and herbs in each bowl, add noodles, then ladle the pork, shrimp and a little broth over. Top with peanuts, crumbled crackers and lime.
nt: Pork and shrimp simmered in a short broth
Best swap: use tofu and mushrooms with vegetable stock for a vegetarian bowl; sesame crackers can replace the rice crackers.

st: Mix the pork with the shallot, [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[1 tbsp]] cornstarch and pepper. Knead 2 minutes until sticky. Roll into 16 small balls.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan over medium heat. Saute the diced tomatoes with [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste for 5 minutes until jammy.
Add [[1 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Drop in the meatballs. Simmer for 15 minutes, turning once, until firm and cooked to 160°F.
Warm the baguettes in a 350°F oven for 5 minutes until crisp.
Split the bread and stuff with 4 meatballs each, a spoon of the sauce, pickles, cucumber and cilantro.
nt: Simmered in tomato sauce
Best swap: use ground chicken or chopped shiitake with tofu. Add a pinch of baking soda to the pork if you want a bouncier ball.

ing: catfish or snakehead, cut in chunks
st: Mix the fish with the turmeric, galangal, fish sauce and yogurt. Marinate 30 minutes in the fridge.
Cook the vermicelli according to the package, rinse with cold water and drain.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pan fry the fish for 3 minutes per side until golden and the center reaches 145°F.
Add the remaining oil, the scallions and a big handful of dill. Toss for 1 minute until just wilted.
Serve right away over vermicelli with the rest of the dill, peanuts and a dip of shrimp paste thinned with lime and water.
nt: Pan fried with turmeric and dill
Best swap: use ginger for galangal 1 to 1, and tilapia or cod for the catfish.
